title: What do a real matcher's mismatches look like: random pixels, near misses, or along the epipolar line?
lede: on a real Middlebury stereo pair SIFT with no ratio test is 56% wrong and 84% of the wrong ones are far, but at a 0.7 ratio test 6% are wrong and 62% of those lie on the true epipolar line (chance: 1%); ten warped photographs give 40% wrong without and 2% with ratio 0.6
summary: sensing-epigate injected mismatches of three invented kinds. This project measures them: OpenCV SIFT on the Middlebury 2014 Motorcycle stereo pair (truth from its disparity map) and on ten scikit-image photographs warped by known homographies, with every wrong match classed as along-epipolar, near (within 40 px) or far. With no ratio test 56% of stereo matches are wrong, 84% of those far; Lowe's ratio test removes the random-looking ones first, so at 0.7 only 6% are wrong but 62% of those lie within 2 px of the true epipolar line (random keypoints land there 1% of the time), the case a single-pair epipolar test cannot reject. Warped photographs: 40% wrong without a ratio test, 2% at 0.6, survivors 12–19% near. Limits: one stereo pair and one detector, ground truth good to about a pixel, class boundaries are mine, not fed back into bundle adjustment.
